subject: Vendor ecosystem stewardship: subprocessor inventory & attestations
messages:
From: Aileen Morris <aileen.morris@healthtech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: updated subprocessor inventory + nested-subprocessor attestations

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement security intake I need an updated subprocessor inventory and brief attestations for any nested (second-tier) subprocessors that process PHI or PII on your behalf. Specifically we need: 

- a CSV of all current subprocessors with their role (hosting, monitoring, analytics, CDNs, etc.) and country of operations;
- for vendors who may process regulated data, a short attestation that they either are SOC 2 Type II covered or operate under appropriate contractual controls (and if so, a pointer to the evidence);
- a one-page SBOM or component summary for client-facing runtime artifacts (or a statement that there are no third-party runtime components beyond open-source libs and their licenses);
- SIG-lite answers or CAIQ export focused on network security, key management, and data residency controls.

We'd like to complete the intake by end of next week (Sep 24). Please let me know if you can provide the CSV and attestations, and whether you need a short call to review. If there are any known gaps (e.g., vendors without SOC reports), flag them and propose mitigations.

Best,
Aileen Morris
Senior Security Manager, HealthTech Systems
attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Aileen Morris <aileen.morris@healthtech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessor inventory + nested-subprocessor attestations

Aileen — thanks for the clear list. We can provide the CSV and attestations but want to confirm the scope so we give you exactly what you need: 

- Do you want the inventory to include transient SaaS dependencies (e.g., frontend error collectors) or only services that handle persisted customer data?
- For SBOM: would a one-page SBOM summary + pointer to the internal bill of materials be sufficient, or do you need the full BOM export?

Plan on our side: I'll coordinate to compile the inventory and a short attestation pack. Marissa will pull the SBOM summary and SIG-lite export; Laura will validate any PCI/PHI-relevant subprocessors and escalate. We aim to deliver an initial packet by Mon Sep 20 and final by Thu Sep 23.

Quick notes we will include so you have visibility: we use KMS-backed encryption at rest for customer-controlled keys where required; TLS 1.3 in transit; and for a subset of customers we offer VPC-private deployment. We'll flag non-SOC vendors and proposed compensating controls (contractual DPA, restricted access, monitoring).

If you'd like a 30-minute sync Monday afternoon to walk the artifacts with Ivan, I'm available 2–4pm PT.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

On Thu, 17 Sep 2026 at 09:12 Aileen Morris <aileen.morris@healthtech.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aileen Morris <aileen.morris@healthtech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessor inventory + nested-subprocessor attestations

Hi Aileen — sending the initial packet for HealthTech review. Files attached and high-level notes below.

Attachments (attached to this message):
- vendor_inventory_q3_2026.csv (CSV): includes vendor name, role, data classification, country, SOC2 status, contract pointer
- sbom_summary_q3_2026.pdf (PDF): one-page SBOM summary for our runtime bundle and list of license types
- sig-lite-answers-sep2026.xlsx (XLSX): filtered SIG-lite answers focused on network/KMS/residency

Highlights / clarifications:
- Scope: the attached inventory includes only subprocessors with access to persisted customer data or production telemetry. We excluded purely marketing/marketing analytics vendors (unless they touch customer telemetry).
- Nested subprocessors: where a vendor delegates (second-tier) processing, we've included a "delegation" column and attached written attestations where available. For example, our logging vendor engages a managed storage backend in EU — attestation included.
- Non-SOC vendors: two smaller CDN edge partners do not maintain SOC 2 reports; for those we have executed DPAs with access restriction clauses and added active monitoring (WAF + egress logs).
- SBOM: summary lists open-source libs and runtime artifacts; no proprietary closed-source runtime dependencies beyond our compiled model bundles.

Next steps: Karthik / Laura will validate any PHI-relevant vendors and confirm encryption and key custody details. If HealthTech needs redacted SOC 2 Type II, we can provide the report through a signed NDA/portal link.

Happy to hop on the call Monday 2:00–2:30pm PT if that helps.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Director, Redwood Inference
attachments: vendor_inventory_q3_2026.csv; sbom_summary_q3_2026.pdf; sig-lite-answers-sep2026.xlsx

From: Aileen Morris <aileen.morris@healthtech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ivan Petrov <ivan.petrov@healthtech.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: updated subprocessor inventory + nested-subprocessor attestations

Marissa / Karthik — received, and thanks for the clear packet. A few quick items: 

- The CSV format works; we downloaded vendor_inventory_q3_2026.csv and will ingest it into our risk tool.
- Please provide a redacted copy of the SOC 2 Type II report (cover pages and control matrix redacted for vendors where allowable) via a secure link. We can provide an NDA or portal access if required.
- We reviewed the SBOM summary; good to see the licensing breakdown. Do you have a full BOM export for the runtime bundle (even if it’s a developer-facing export)? That will speed our legal review.
- For the two non-SOC CDN partners: please confirm the DPA reference IDs for our intake form — if you can paste the clause name/paragraph number that would be helpful.

We are OK to proceed to procurement approval on the basis of these artifacts plus the SOC redactions. Let's plan a 30-minute follow-up on Mon Sep 21 11am PT to close any outstanding acceptance items (Ivan will join). If you can upload the SOC link before then, that would be great.

Regards,
Aileen Morris
Senior Security Manager, HealthTech Systems
attachments: none
